source_text: Ἐπὶ δὲ τούτοις τεθαῤῥηκότες, οὐ μεῖον ἢ τοῖς ἤδη γενομένοις, καὶ τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἐπισκοποῦντες φύσιν, τήν τε μετ᾿ ἐνδείας καὶ φθορᾶς ζωὴν στέργομεν, ὡς τῷ παρόντι βίῳ προσήκουσαν, καὶ τὴν ἐν ἐφθαρσίᾳ διαμονὴν ἐλπίζομεν βεβαίως· ἣν οὐ παρ᾿ ἀνθρώπων ἀναπλάττομεν μάτην, ψευδέσιν ἑαυτοὺς βουκολοῦντες ἐλπίσιν, ἀπλανεστάτῳ δὲ πεπιστεύκαμεν ἐχεγγύῳ, τῇ τοῦ δημιουργήσαντος ἡμᾶς γνώμῃ, καθ᾿ ἣν ἐποίησεν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ ψυχῆς ἀθανάτου καὶ σώματος, νοῦν τε συγκατεσκεύασεν αὐτῷ καὶ νόμον ἔμφυτον ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ καὶ φυλακῇ τῶν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ δεδομένων, ἔμφρονί τε βίῳ καὶ ζωῇ λογικῇ προσηκόντων, εὖ εἰδότες ὡς οὐκ ἂν τοιοῦτον κατεσκεύασε ζῶον καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς πρὸς διαμονὴν ἐκόσμησεν, εἰ μὴ διαμένειν ἐβούλετο τὸ γενόμενον. Εἰ τοίνυν ὁ τοῦδε τοῦ παντὸς δημιουργὸς ἐποίησεν ἄνθρωπον ἐπὶ τῷ ζωῆς ἔμφρονος μετασχεῖν, καὶ γενόμενον θεωρὸν τῆς τε μεγαλοπρεπείας αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ πᾶσι σοφίας τῇ τούτων συνδιαμένειν ἀεὶ θεωρίᾳ, κατὰ τὴν ἐκείνου γνώμην καὶ καθ᾿ ἣν εἴληχε φύσιν, ἡ μὲν τῆς γενέσεως αἰτία πιστοῦται τὴν εἰς ἀεὶ διαμονήν, ἡ δὲ διαμονὴ τὴν ἀνάστασιν, ἧς χωρὶς οὐκ ἂν διαμείνειεν ἄνθρωπος. Ἐκ δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων εὔδηλον ὡς τῇ τῆς γενέσεως αἰτίᾳ καὶ τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ ποιήσαντος δείκνυται σαφῶς ἡ ἀνάστασις. Τοιαύτης δὲ τῆς αἰτίας οὔσης, καθ᾿ ἣν εἰς τόνδε παρῆκται τὸν κόσμον ἄνθρωπος, ἀκόλουθον ἂν εἴη τὸν τούτοις κατὰ φύσιν ἢ καθ᾿ εἱρμὸν ἑπόμενον διασκέψασθαι λόγον· ἕπεται δὲ κατὰ τὴν ἐξέτασιν τῇ μὲν αἰτίᾳ τῆς γενέσεως ἡ τῶν γεννηθέντων ἀνθρώπων φύσις, τῇ δὲ φύσει τῶν γενομένων ἡ τοῦ ποιήσαντος ἐπὶ τούτοις δικαία κρίσις, τούτοις τε πᾶσι τὸ τοῦ βίου τέλος. Ἐξητασμένων δὲ ἡμῖν τῶν προτεταγμένων ἐπισκεπτέον ἑξῆς τὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων φύσιν.
thought_title: The cause of creation proves resurrection
orientation: Athenagoras has just finished arguing that resurrection is possible for God and not blocked by objections about bodies eaten by animals; now he begins the positive argument from God's purpose in creating human beings.
pass_a_gloss: And having taken courage in these things, no less than in the things already accomplished, and examining our own nature, we both love the life with want and corruption, as befitting the present life, and we hope firmly for the continuance in incorruptibility; which we do not fabricate in vain from humans, deceiving ourselves with false hopes, but we have trusted in a most unerring guarantee, the purpose of the one who made us, according to which he made man from immortal soul and body, and he equipped him with mind and an innate law for the safety and guarding of the things given by him, things befitting intelligent life and rational living, knowing well that he would not have constructed such a living creature and adorned it with all things for continuance, if he did not wish the thing that came to be to continue. If therefore the maker of this universe made man for the purpose of sharing in intelligent life, and made him, when he came to be, a beholder of his magnificence and of his wisdom over all things, to continue always with the contemplation of these things, according to that one's purpose and according to the nature which he obtained, the cause of his coming to be guarantees the continuance forever, and the continuance guarantees the resurrection, without which man would not continue. And from the things said it is very clear that by the cause of his coming to be and by the purpose of the maker the resurrection is shown clearly. And since the cause is of such a kind, according to which man has been brought into this world, it would be consistent to examine the argument that follows these things according to nature or according to sequence; and there follows, according to the examination, to the cause of coming to be the nature of the human beings who have been born, and to the nature of those who have come to be the just judgment of the maker upon these things, and to all these things the end of life. And since the things set before have been examined by us, we must examine next the nature of human beings.

lemmas.gloss: we love, we are content with

choices.why: Keeps the glossary terms 'continuance' for διαμονή and 'incorruptibility' for ἀφθαρσία, preserving the technical force of the argument.

choices.english: the purpose of the one who made us
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'purpose' for γνώμη and renders the participle literally as 'the one who made us' to keep the agent explicit.
rejected: the intention of the one who fashioned us

choices.why: Literal rendering preserving the preposition ἐκ and the glossary terms 'soul' and 'body'; the immortality of the soul is explicit in the source.
rejected: of an immortal soul and a body

choices.term: νοῦν τε συγκατεσκεύασεν αὐτῷ καὶ νόμον ἔμφυτον
choices.english: and he equipped him with mind and an innate law
choices.why: Keeps the compound verb's force ('equipped together with') and renders ἔμφυτον as 'innate' to preserve the idea of a law built into human nature.
rejected: and he furnished him with intellect and a natural law
and he gave him reason and an implanted law

choices.term: θεωρὸν τῆς τε μεγαλοπρεπείας αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ πᾶσι σοφίας
choices.english: a beholder of his magnificence and of his wisdom over all things
choices.why: Renders θεωρός as 'beholder' to keep the contemplative sense, and preserves the two genitives of the things beheld.
rejected: a spectator of his majesty and wisdom in all things
an observer of his greatness and universal wisdom

choices.term: ἡ μὲν τῆς γενέσεως αἰτία πιστοῦται τὴν εἰς ἀεὶ διαμονήν
choices.english: the cause of his coming to be guarantees the continuance forever
choices.why: Keeps the causal language literal ('cause of coming to be') and renders πιστοῦται as 'guarantees' to convey the strong epistemic force.
rejected: the reason for his origin confirms his everlasting continuance
the cause of his birth assures his permanence forever

pass_b_english: We take courage from these things no less than from what has already happened, and we also examine our own nature. We embrace the life that involves need and decay, since it belongs to this present existence, and we firmly hope for continuance in incorruptibility. We do not invent this hope from human sources, deceiving ourselves with empty expectations. Rather, we have trusted in a most unerring guarantee: the purpose of the one who made us. According to that purpose, God made the human being from immortal soul and body. He also equipped the human being with mind and an innate law for salvation and for the keeping of what God had given, gifts suited to a rational life and an intelligent way of living. We know well that God would not have fashioned such a living creature and adorned it with everything needed for continuance unless he willed that what came into being should continue.

If, then, the maker of this universe made the human being in order to partake of intelligent life, and made him a beholder of God's magnificence and of his wisdom over all things so that he might continue forever in the contemplation of these things, according to the maker's purpose and the nature he received, then the cause of his coming to be vouches for continuance forever, and continuance vouches for the resurrection, without which a human being could not continue. From what has been said, it is quite clear that the resurrection is plainly demonstrated by the cause of his coming to be and by the purpose of the one who made him.

Since this is the cause for which the human being has been brought into this world, it would be fitting to examine the argument that follows from this by nature and in due order. In this examination, next after the cause of coming to be comes the nature of human beings who have been born. What follows the nature of those who have come to be is the just judgment of the maker concerning these things. And what follows all these is the end of life. Since the matters set out first have been examined by us, we must next consider the nature of human beings.

problems.quote: We are content with the life that involves need and decay
problems.source_quote: τὴν μετ᾿ ἐνδείας καὶ φθορᾶς ζωὴν στέργομεν
problems.why: στέργομεν means 'we love/are devoted to', not 'are content with'; active affection, not resignation
problems.fix: We embrace the life that involves need and decay

problems.quote: he equipped him with mind and an innate law for the preservation and protection of the gifts he had given
problems.source_quote: νοῦν τε συγκατεσκεύασεν αὐτῷ καὶ νόμον ἔμφυτον ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ καὶ φυλακῇ τῶν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ δεδομένων
problems.why: ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ means 'for salvation', not 'preservation'; σωτηρία is salvation/deliverance, not mere keeping safe
problems.fix: for salvation and the keeping of the gifts he had given

problems.quote: He knew well that he would not have fashioned
problems.source_quote: εὖ εἰδότες ὡς οὐκ ἂν τοιοῦτον κατεσκεύασε
problems.why: εὖ εἰδότες is nominative plural, referring to 'we' (the author and readers), not 'he'; participial construction with main verb understood
problems.fix: well knowing that he would not have fashioned

problems.quote: the maker of this universe made the human being to share in intelligent life
problems.source_quote: ἐποίησεν ἄνθρωπον ἐπὶ τῷ ζωῆς ἔμφρονος μετασχεῖν
problems.why: ἐπὶ τῷ with infinitive expresses purpose, but 'to share in' weakens μετασχεῖν which means 'to partake of/have a share in'; more importantly, the Greek emphasizes the purpose for which
problems.fix: the maker of this universe made the human being in order to partake of intelligent life

problems.quote: so that he might remain forever in the contemplation of these things
problems.why: συνδιαμένειν means 'to remain together with' or 'to continue with', not 'remain in'; the prefix συν- is significant, implying enduring alongside or in company with
problems.fix: so that he might continue forever in the contemplation of these things

problems.quote: the cause of his coming to be guarantees the continuance forever
problems.source_quote: ἡ μὲν τῆς γενέσεως αἰτία πιστοῦται τὴν εἰς ἀεὶ διαμονήν
problems.why: πιστοῦται means 'gives assurance of' or 'pledges', not 'guarantees' in the sense of ensuring; it's a weaker, more testimonial sense
problems.fix: the cause of his coming to be gives assurance of continuance forever

problems.why: Same issue: πιστοῦται is understood from previous clause, meaning 'gives assurance of', not 'guarantees'
problems.fix: the continuance gives assurance of the resurrection

problems.quote: what follows the cause of coming to be is the nature of the human beings who have been born
problems.source_quote: τῇ μὲν αἰτίᾳ τῆς γενέσεως ἡ τῶν γεννηθέντων ἀνθρώπων φύσις
problems.why: ἕπεται is understood: 'what follows from...is', but more precisely 'next after the cause of coming to be comes the nature'
problems.fix: next after the cause of coming to be comes the nature of human beings who have been born

problems.quote: the just judgment of the maker upon them
problems.source_quote: ἡ τοῦ ποιήσαντος ἐπὶ τούτοις δικαία κρίσις
problems.why: ἐπὶ τούτοις means 'concerning these things' or 'in these matters', not 'upon them' (which would be κατ᾿ αὐτῶν or similar); misread of ἐπί
problems.fix: the just judgment of the maker concerning these things

problems.quote: Since we have examined the matters set out first, we must next consider the nature of human beings
problems.source_quote: Ἐξητασμένων δὲ ἡμῖν τῶν προτεταγμένων ἐπισκεπτέον ἑξῆς τὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων φύσιν
problems.why: Ἐξητασμένων δὲ ἡμῖν is genitive absolute: 'Since the matters set out first have been examined by us', but the English loses the passive/absolute construction; more importantly, 'we must next consider' for ἐπισκεπτέον is fine, but the Greek emphasizes 'it remains to be considered'
problems.fix: Since the matters set out first have been examined by us, we must next consider the nature of human beings

last_rejected.quote: We embrace the life that involves need and decay
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν μετ᾿ ἐνδείας καὶ φθορᾶς ζωὴν στέργομεν
last_rejected.why: στέργομεν means 'we are content with'/'we accept', not 'embrace' which suggests active affection.
last_rejected.fix: We are content with the life that involves need and decay
last_rejected.ruling: στέργομεν denotes love/affection; 'embrace' is within its semantic range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: he equipped him with mind and an innate law for salvation and the keeping of what he had given
last_rejected.source_quote: νοῦν τε συγκατεσκεύασεν αὐτῷ καὶ νόμον ἔμφυτον ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ καὶ φυλακῇ τῶν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ δεδομένων
last_rejected.why: ἐπί + dative indicates purpose/result: 'for the purpose of salvation and the keeping of...' The English makes 'salvation and keeping' the object of 'for', but the Greek has 'for salvation' and 'for the keeping of what was given'.
last_rejected.fix: he furnished him with mind and an innate law for salvation and for keeping what he had given
last_rejected.ruling: English 'for salvation and the keeping of' accurately renders ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ καὶ φυλακῇ; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: made him a beholder of his magnificence and of his wisdom over all things so that he might continue forever in the contemplation of these things
last_rejected.source_quote: γενόμενον θεωρὸν τῆς τε μεγαλοπρεπείας αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ πᾶσι σοφίας τῇ τούτων συνδιαμένειν ἀεὶ θεωρίᾳ
last_rejected.why: τῇ...θεωρίᾳ is dative of manner/instrument, not purpose: 'by/in the contemplation of these things' he continues, not 'so that he might continue in contemplation'.
last_rejected.fix: made him a beholder of his magnificence and of his wisdom over all things, to continue forever by the contemplation of these things
last_rejected.ruling: τῇ τούτων συνδιαμένειν ἀεὶ θεωρίᾳ: 'so that he might continue in contemplation' captures purpose and dative adequately.

last_rejected.quote: the cause of his coming to be vouches for continuance forever
last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ μὲν τῆς γενέσεως αἰτία πιστοῦται τὴν εἰς ἀεὶ διαμονήν
last_rejected.why: εἰς ἀεί = 'for ever'/'to eternity', but 'continuance forever' blurs that this is continuance into eternity, not merely unending duration.
last_rejected.fix: the cause of his coming to be guarantees continuance to eternity
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς ἀεὶ διαμονήν rendered 'continuance forever' is accurate; no meaningful distinction lost.

polish.changed: Clarified who acts and who is spoken about, made God the explicit subject where the source implies it, smoothed sentence order, and removed awkward phrasing while preserving every claim and qualification.

variants.text: the continuance of the body according to its own nature

notes.why: Different phrases for the same concept of ongoing existence after resurrection.
notes.fix: Use one term or signal these are synonymous.
